facts.fact: RMS Titanic sank on 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg, resulting in approximately 1,500 deaths.
Titanic had advanced safety features like watertight compartments and remotely activated doors, but these failed to prevent its sinking.
Titanic carried 20 lifeboats, accommodating 1,178 people, but only 705 passengers and crew survived.
Water temperatures at −2 °C during the sinking caused hypothermia, killing most in 15–30 minutes.
The Grand Staircase was destroyed during the sinking, with the structure likely ejected upwards through its dome.
Watertight bulkheads on Titanic extended to eight of the fifteen bulkheads, but flooding overwhelmed them.
Regulations required 16 lifeboats for 990 occupants, but White Star Line provided 20 lifeboats for 1,178 people.

sentences.text: What would it feel like to be on the Titanic as it sank?
You board the RMS Titanic, unaware of the iceberg ahead.
A loud crash shakes the ship as it hits an iceberg.
Passengers scream as water floods the lower decks, breaching watertight bulkheads.
The ship splits in two, destroying the Grand Staircase.
